card.title: Planes — normal form to point distance

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Space lines need direction cosines (l, m, n with l²+m²+n² = 1) or free ratios (a, b, c); symmetric form (x−x₀)/a = (y−y₀)/b = (z−z₀)/c walks the line. Planes pivot on their NORMAL: normal form lx+my+nz = p, general ax+by+c+d = 0 with (a,b,c) as normal ratios. Angles come from dot products (line–line, plane–plane via normals, line–plane as complement); point-to-plane distance drops perpendicularly.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: l² + m² + n² = 1 (cosines) · ratios scale freely  ·  line: (x−x₀)/a = (y−y₀)/b = (z−z₀)/c  ·  plane: lx+my+nz = p · ax+by+cz+d = 0  ·  cosθ = |a₁a₂+b₁b₂+c₁c₂|/(magnitudes)  ·  distance point→plane: |ax₀+by₀+cz₀+d|/√(a²+b²+c²)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: Direction cosines must normalise (ratios need not). Symmetric line form needs all denominators non-zero (zero denominator = parallel to that axis plane — handle separately). Plane distance formula needs the general form (move everything left first). Angle formulas give acute values via absolute value.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Line parallel to a plane: direction ⊥ normal (dot = 0). Two planes perpendicular: normals perpendicular (a₁a₂+b₁b₂+c₁c₂ = 0). Skew lines (non-parallel, non-intersecting) need shortest-distance machinery. Coordinate planes: x = 0 (yz), y = 0 (xz), z = 0 (xy).

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Distance from (1, 2, 3) to 2x − y + 2z = 5: rewrite 2x − y + 2z − 5 = 0 → |2(1) − 2 + 2(3) − 5|/√(4+1+4) = |2−2+6−5|/3 = 1/3. One substitution into the formula — the normal (2,−1,2) does all the work.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Direction-cosine uniqueness fails (two sign choices per line). Symmetric form breaks for axis-parallel lines (zero denominators need parametric fallback). Distance formulas measure perpendicular separation only — askew configurations need the full shortest-distance treatment.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: Plane from perpendicularity: points X with (X − X₀)·n̂ = 0 → lx+my+nz = p (normal form); scaling gives general form. Line symmetric form eliminates the parameter t from x = x₀+at, y = y₀+bt, z = z₀+ct. Point–plane distance: project the joining vector onto the unit normal — absolute projection is the formula.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Read normals straight off plane equations (coefficients = normal ratios). Angles: dot the directions (lines) or normals (planes). Distance: substitute point, absolute value, divide by normal's magnitude. Parallelism/perpendicularity: dot = 0 vs ratios proportional.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: NEB-style: line in symmetric form from two points; plane through three points; angle between lines/planes; point-to-plane distance numerical; parallelism/perpendicularity verdicts.
